problems.title: Difference of squares
problems.question: Find(x+y)² if x²−y²=28 and x−y=4.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: x²−y²=(x−y)(x+y).
steps: Thus x+y=28/4=7, and its square is 49.

problems.title: Median and bisector in a right triangle
problems.question: The median and bisector from a right-angle vertex make25°. Find the larger acute angle.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The bisector makes45° with either leg. The hypotenuse midpoint has coordinates(a/2, b/2), so the median direction makes one of the triangle’s acute angles with a leg.
steps: That angle differs from 45° by 25°, giving20° or 70°. The larger acute angle is 70°.

problems.title: Equal absolute values
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of|2x−3|=|x−9|.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Equality gives 2x−3=x−9 or 2x−3=−x+9.
steps: The roots are −6 and 4, sum −2.

problems.title: Distance between clock-hand tips
problems.question: Clock hands have lengths 6 cm,4 cm. Find their tip separation at 2:00.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The angle is 60°; d²=6²+4²−2·6·4cos60°.
steps: Thus d²=28, d=2√7 cm.

problems.title: Rhombus height
problems.question: A rhombus has diagonals6,8. Find its height.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
steps: Height=are a/side=24/5=4.8.

problems.title: Internal common tangent length
problems.question: Two circles have radii3,4 and centre distance 5√2. Find the internal common tangent segment.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: L²=d²−(R+r)².

problems.title: Find a false implication
problems.question: Which statement is false:−2<x<3 implies4<x²<9; x<y implies x−y<0;|x|<3 implies−3<x<3; x<−3 implies x²>9?
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Test the first implication with x=0.
steps: Its premise holds but4<x² fails. The other three follow directly from subtraction, absolute-value definition, and squaring a number with magnitude>3.

problems.title: Length of an angle bisector
problems.question: A triangle has sides 4,5,6. Find the bisector to side 6.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: l²=bc[1−a²/(b+c)²], with a=6, b=4, c=5.

problems.title: Incircle of an isosceles triangle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base6 and legs5. Find inradius.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Height=√(25−9)=4, are a 12, semiperimeter8.
steps: r=are a/semiperimeter=12/8=1.5.

problems.title: A parallel line through a point
problems.question: Find the line through(2,3) parallel to y=2x+1.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Parallel lines have the same slope2.
steps: Use y−3=2(x−2), giving y=2x−1.

problems.title: An impossible radical equality
problems.question: Count roots of √(4x²−4x+1)=2x−5.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The left side is|2x−1|. The right side must be≥0, so x≥2.5.
steps: On this range|2x−1|=2x−1, which cannot equal2x−5.

problems.title: A rational inequality
problems.question: Solve x/(x−4)<1/3.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Move terms to obtain2(x+2)/[3(x−4)]<0.
steps: The quotient is negative between−2 and 4. Both endpoints are excluded.

problems.title: Bounds on a reciprocal difference
problems.question: Given3<a<4,5<b<6, find the range of 1/a−1/b and the listed interval containing all values.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
steps: Subtract the extreme bounds to obtain1/20<1/a−1/b<1/6.
Among the offered intervals, only(1/21,1/5) contains this entire range.

problems.title: Distance from a centre to a chord
problems.question: A diameter crosses a chord at angleα, dividing the chord into15 and 7. Given tanα=2, find the centre-to-chord distance.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The crossing is(15−7)/2=4 from the chord midpoint. The radius to that midpoint is perpendicular to the chord.
steps: In the resulting right triangle, tanα=distance/4. Hence distance 8.

problems.title: Translate a quadratic graph
problems.question: Translate y=2x²+8x+5 right3 and down2.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The new function is f(x−3)−2.

problems.title: Recover coefficients from a positivity interval
problems.question: The solution of −x²+ax+b>0 is(−7,4). Find a+b.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The polynomial is −(x+7)(x−4)=−x²−3x+28.
steps: Thus a=−3, b=28, and a+b=25.

problems.title: Inradius-to-circumradius ratio
problems.question: Find r/R for an isosceles right triangle.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: For legs s, hypotenuse s√2, r=s(2−√2)/2, R=s√2/2.
steps: Divide to get r/R=√2−1=1/(1+√2).

problems.title: Radius from two tangents
problems.question: Tangents MA, MB for m angleα, and chord AB=b. Find circle radius.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The central angle AOB is 180°−α. Chord b=2R sin((180°−α)/2)=2Rcos(α/2).
steps: Solve for R=b/[2cos(α/2)].

problems.title: A diameter circle finds an altitude
problems.question: ABC is right at C, BC=a, AC=b. The circle with diameter BC meets AB again at K. Find CK.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Thales’ theorem makes∠BKC=90°, so CK is the altitude to hypotenuse AB.
steps: Equating areas gives CK=ab/√(a²+b²).

problems.title: Sum of side squares from a median
problems.question: A triangle has BC=4 and median from A of length 3. Find AB²+AC².
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Apollonius:AB²+AC²=2m²+BC²/2.
steps: The value is 2·9+16/2=26.

problems.title: Cancel a factor but retain its exclusion
problems.question: Solve[(x−5)²(x+7)]/[(x−5)(x+4)]≤0.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The original excludes x=5,−4. Else the expression is(x−5)(x+7)/(x+4).
steps: A sign chart at −7,−4,5 gives(−∞,−7]∪(−4,5). The cancelled zero5 remains excluded.

problems.title: A quadratic in a square
problems.question: Find the product of real roots of(x²+2x+1)²−5(x+1)²−6=0.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Put t=(x+1)²≥0. Then(t−6)(t+1)=0, so t=6.
steps: The real roots are −1±√6, whose product is 1−6=−5.

problems.title: Zero product of radicals
problems.question: Count real roots of √(x²+5x)·√(x²+3x)=0.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The shared domain is x≤−5 or x≥0. Possible zeros are −5,−3,0.
steps: Only −5 and 0 lie in the shared domain.

problems.title: Exactly five integer system solutions
problems.question: Find a such that x²+7x−8<0 and|x|<a have exactly 5 integer solutions.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The first inequality is −8<x<1, whose integers are −7,…,0.
steps: To include0,−1,−2,−3,−4 but exclude−5, require4<a≤5.

problems.title: A cancelled factor can destroy evenness
problems.question: Which is not even:|x|−1,(x−x³)/x,[(x−1)(x²+1)]/(x−1),√x²?
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: An even function needs both f(−x)=f(x) and a symmetric domain.
steps: The third simplifies to x²+1 but excludes x=1; its domain contains−1 without1. It is therefore not even. The second excludes0 symmetrically and remains even.

problems.title: Inequalities for all real inputs
problems.question: Which always hold:1)a²+b²≥2ab;2)(a+b)/2≥√(ab);3)a²+ab+b²≥0?
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: 1 follows from(a−b)²≥0;3 follows from(a+b/2)²+3b²/4≥0.
steps: Statement2 fails for a=b=−1, and its radical is not even real when ab<0.

problems.title: Two perpendicular medians
problems.question: Two medians of lengths 9,12 are perpendicular. Find the third median.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: At the centroid, the corresponding vertex vectors are perpendicular with lengths 6,8. The third vertex vector is their negative sum.
steps: Its length is √(6²+8²)=10. The third median is 3/2 times that, or 15.

problems.title: Orthogonal trapezoid diagonals
problems.question: The perpendicular diagonals of a trapezoid have squared-length sum 16. Find its midline.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Let diagonal vectors u, v be oriented from the same base toward the other. Their difference is parallel to the bases with length a+b.
steps: Since u·v=0,(a+b)²=|u−v|²=|u|²+|v|²=16. Thus midline(a+b)/2=2.

problems.title: Choose an input for a composite function
problems.question: Given f((x+3)/(1−x))=x/2, find f(3).
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
steps: It gives x=0, which is allowed. Then f(3)=0/2=0.

problems.title: Quadratic roots of opposite signs
problems.question: For which a do the roots of x²−2ax+a²−4=0 have opposite signs?
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The roots are a−2 and a+2. Their product a²−4 must be strictly negative.
steps: Thus−2<a<2. At either endpoint one root is 0 and is neither positive nor negative.
problems.note: The listed choice[−2,2] incorrectly includes endpoints; none of the listed sets is exactly correct.

problems.title: Leg from its hypotenuse projection
problems.question: In a right triangle, altitude foot H has BH=1 and BC=3. Find the other leg AC.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: BC²=AB·BH gives AB=9.
steps: Then AC=√(AB²−BC²)=√(81−9)=6√2.

problems.title: Two bounds force equality
problems.question: Solve−(x+1)²+2=(x−2)²/9+9/(x−2)².
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The left side is≤2. The right side is u+1/u≥2 for u=(x−2)²/9>0.
steps: Equality requires x=−1 on the left, and u=1 on the right. x=−1 satisfies both, so it is the unique root.

problems.title: Squares on right-triangle legs
problems.question: External squares ACDE, BCFG are built on legs1,4. The line of the median from C meets FD at N. Find CN.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Use C=(0,0), A=(a,0), B=(0, b), D=(0,−a), F=(−b,0). The median line is(x, y)=t(a, b).
steps: FD has equation x/b+y/a=−1. Thus t=−ab/(a²+b²), and CN=|t|√(a²+b²)=ab/√(a²+b²).
With a=1, b=4, this is 4/√17.
problems.note: This uses the standard external-square construction and the extended median line.

problems.title: Count intersections of a line and a conic
problems.question: Count solution pairs of 4x²+1=y²+4x, y−x=3.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Substitute y=x+3 to get3x²−10x−8=0.
steps: Its discriminant100+96=196>0, so there are 2 distinct x-values, each with one y.

problems.title: Exactly three nested-absolute-value roots
problems.question: Find a for which||x+4|−7|=a has exactly 3 roots.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Let u=|x+4|≥0. Then u=7±a. A positive u gives 2 roots, u=0 gives 1.
steps: Exactly3 roots occur when one u is 0 and the other positive: a=7, giving u=0,14.

problems.title: A median meets the circumcircle
problems.question: The median from A meets the circumcircle again at D. AC=CD=1. Find BC.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Let M be midpoint BC, AM=p, MD=q, BM=CM=t. Circle power gives pq=t².
steps: Apply Stewart to isosceles triangle ACD with cevian CM:1=t²+pq. Hence1=2t².
Thus BC=2t=√2.

problems.title: Inradii of altitude subtriangles
problems.question: The altitude to a right triangle’s hypotenuse creates triangles with inradii3,5. Find the original inradius.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The two smaller triangles are similar to the original, with linear scales leg₁/hypotenuse and leg₂/hypotenuse.
steps: These squared scales sum 1 by Pythagoras. Inradii scale linearly, so r²=3²+5²=34.

problems.title: Teacher and class average ages
problems.question: A teacher is 24 years older than the student average and 20 older than the average of everyone in the room. How many students?
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: If the student average is m, the teacher is m+24 and the overall average is m+4.
steps: With n students,(nm+m+24)/(n+1)=m+4. Thus24=4(n+1), giving n=5.

problems.title: Obtuse triangles with integer sides
problems.question: An obtuse triangle has integer sides and two sides 3,4. Find all possible sines of its largest angle.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The third side c is an integer with 1<c<7, so c=2,3,4,5,6.
steps: Only c=2 and 6 give obtuse triangles;3,4 give acute triangles and 5 gives a right triangle.
For c=2, the angle opposite4 has cosine−1/4, sine√15/4. For c=6, the largest cosine is(9+16−36)/24=−11/24, sine√455/24.

problems.title: An ambiguous side-side-angle triangle
problems.question: D is the midpoint of arc BC not containing A, and AD meets BC at K. Given AC=21, BC=24, cos∠ABC=11/14, find AD.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: Let c=AB. The cosine rule gives 7c²−264c+945=0, so c=(132±3√1201)/7. Both positive roots give valid triangles.
steps: Because BD=CD, Ptolemy gives AD·BC=BD(AB+AC). With the chord formulas, this becomes AD²=21c(21+c)²/[(21+c)²−24²].
For the two allowed c-values, AD≈29.6073 or 32.6786 cm.
problems.answer: Two possible lengths, approximately 29.6073 cm and 32.6786 cm.
problems.note: The printed conditions do not select a unique triangle. The formulas above give exact lengths by substituting either exact c-value; the usual arc BC excluding A is used.

problems.title: Minimize the distance between quadratic roots
problems.question: For x²+(a−2)x−2a−15=0, find a minimizing the distance between roots.
problems.idea: Reduce the given conditions using a standard identity or geometric theorem.
formulas: The discriminant is(a−2)²+8a+60=(a+2)²+60. Root separation is its square root.
steps: This is minimized when a+2=0, so a=−2. The minimum separation is √60.
